name: insolvia-design-system-workspace
//: Root of the design-system npm workspace. NOT a shippable package — it
declares the members and pins the shared toolchain.
Two members, BOTH published to GitHub Packages:
They were extracted from insolvia-ai/insolvia, where the design system was
a workspace member the app consumed by SYMLINK — so a design-system change
reached the app with no publish and no version bump. That is the coupling
this repo exists to remove: there is now exactly one channel out of here,
the registry, and every consumer travels it.
tokens is published rather than private (it was private in the monorepo)
because it no longer shares a workspace with its consumers. The app and
the Cognito branding generator in insolvia-ai/insolvia both install it.
The member list is EXPLICIT and must stay that way — never `packages/*`.
Adding a member silently gives it a symlink to the other's source, which
is how a broken package passes CI here and only breaks after publishing.

//scripts: Script commentary lives HERE, beside `scripts`, and never inside it.
The monorepo this came from puts `//name` comment keys among the scripts
themselves, which npm tolerates. Storybook does not: its build walks the
`scripts` object calling `.match()` on every value, so an array-valued
comment key crashes it with `TypeError: s?.match is not a function` —
from `computeStorybookMetadata`, naming neither package.json nor the key,
and not skippable with `--disable-telemetry`. Ten minutes to find, once.
Keeping the comments as arrays (readable, multi-line) but moving them out
of `scripts` costs only adjacency, and this object sits immediately above
tokens: Run with plain `node`, no loader and no build step: Node >=24 strips
TypeScript types natively, so the generator stays dependency-free.

The generator renders tokens.json into this repo's two outputs. The
THIRD output it used to write — Cognito's managed-login branding under
infra/ — stayed behind in insolvia-ai/insolvia, which now reconciles it
against the published @insolvia-ai/tokens instead. Adding an output that
writes outside this repo is what that split exists to prevent.
lint: Fans out per member rather than running ESLint once from the root, and
there is deliberately NO `eslint.config.js` at the repo root — the rules
live in `eslint.base.js`, which each member re-exports. ESLint discovers
a flat config by walking UP from its cwd, so a root one is also found by
any subdirectory with its own ESLint setup. Read eslint.base.js before
ci: The whole local gate: token drift, format, lint, typecheck, test.
Mirrors what .github/workflows/pr.yml runs, so `npm run ci` green
locally is a fair predictor of a green PR. It does NOT build the
workbench — CI does that separately, because it is slower than the rest
of the gate put together and breaks far less often.
storybook: The component workbench: the only place a component is LOOKED AT rather
than asserted about. `storybook` is the dev loop (./scripts/dev-up.sh
wraps it); `storybook:build` produces the static site CI builds to prove
the workbench still compiles. Read .storybook/main.ts before changing
either — it explains why the React Native Web framework renders BOTH
leaves, and workbench/react-native.ts explains the one export it

scripts.ci: npm run tokens:check && npm run format && npm run lint && npm run typecheck && npm run test && npm run test:a11y

//devDependencies: these packages are linted and typechecked here but CONSUMED there, and two
toolchain majors across the boundary would mean source that passes here and
fails in the consumer. TypeScript is 5.9 rather than the 7.x line:
`erasableSyntaxOnly` (5.8+) is the feature this workspace depends on.
